import.policy: verbatim import; narrow, story-documented deviations listed under 'deviations' — shipped 4.8.1 binaries outrank the published snapshot when they measurably disagree (PROJECT.md authority order)
import.verification: Files not named under 'deviations' must match upstream.sourceTree; deviating files are accounted for individually.

deviations.reason: SaveAs rooted-path guard (ledger P50)
request-cookie configured defaults; shipped 4.8.1 (System.Web 4.8.9319.0) carries a servicing fix absent from every published source branch, ported from IL readings

backmerged from upstream branch NetFramework48ZDP (e47d8c1b6482e0babe243dff2f9ece1507c814ff): SameSiteMode ConvertTo fix and cookieSameSite doc-comment corrections; the branch's comment-scrubber hunk in Util/AppSettings.cs was deliberately not taken
Dynamic Data enablement guarded behind a resolvable-type probe; System.Web.DynamicData is not carried (ledger P69)
case-folding the configuration system's mapped directory, composed web.config name, and the configSource path System.Configuration composes below them, on a case-sensitive filesystem (ledger P70)
the typed WebServices getter would recreate Framework's System.Web <-> System.Web.Services assembly cycle; it returns ConfigurationSection here (ADR-0009 amendment)
WorkItem.Post refused every non-Win32NT platform, a Win9x-era guard; the post lands on the ordinary thread pool, so the guard is fenced NETFRAMEWORK for one-way web methods off Windows

SetConfigurationFilePaths seam (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): the host publishes the machine/root config locations at bootstrap; the Framework fallback resolves against MsCorLibDirectory, which has no Config subdirectory on modern .NET, breaking consumers such as the WSDL help page path

the deserialization ctor chains to ClaimsPrincipal(SerializationInfo, StreamingContext), a throwing stub on modern .NET (SYSLIB0051); the base call is fenced NETFRAMEWORK and a payload guard refuses anything but a role-cookie ticket

AddIdentityAttachingRoles builds a DeferredRoleClaimsIdentity (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK) because ClaimsIdentity.ExternalClaims holds List<Claim> on modern .NET where Framework held IEnumerable<Claim>, so role claims cannot be parked unevaluated on a stock ClaimsIdentity

the validators are written as plain headers and the cache policy is left untouched (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK), because IIS's native static module owned these responses and sent no Cache-Control and no Expires without a caching profile; an unmodified policy is also never stored by OutputCacheModule, which is what the retired SetNoServerCaching call had arranged

the classic header generation honors SuppressDefaultCacheControlHeader (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK) as the integrated one already did, since the host replaces IIS's native static module and its responses carry no Cache-Control at all

the module collection is built from the merged system.webServer/modules snapshot through the integrated-mode builder already present here, with per-request managedHandler conditioning wrapped around the classic execution steps (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK), its answer settled once from the URL as it arrived and held on the context for the rest of the request, and the classic UrlMappingsExecutionStep retired in favour of the golden's UrlMappingsModule row

the golden registers this module in every application, so the anonymous WindowsIdentity/WindowsPrincipal statics move into a nested holder that defers their platform failure, and IsEnabled answers false (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK) rather than the authentication section's default, which is Windows

handler selection walks the merged system.webServer/handlers snapshot instead of the classic <httpHandlers> mapping (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): MapHttpHandler asks the walk for the handler and keeps the factory-recycling bookkeeping around it, and AssemblyResourceLoader asks the same list whether WebResource.axd is still mapped to it

IIS request filtering's <fileExtensions> deny list is checked beside the hidden-segment rule in ValidatePath (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK), because the retired classic <httpHandlers> table was what had been refusing those extensions; both refusals are native responses that end the request without a managed exception (ledger P97)

with the shipped classic <httpModules> table retired, InitModules publishes the merged module list through IntegratedModuleList, which only IIS's native wireup used to fill, and UrlAuthorizationModule.CheckUrlAccessForPrincipal reads it instead of scanning the classic section (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK)

RaiseRuntimeError writes the raised error to WebFormsRuntimeEventSource before the HealthMonitoringManager.Enabled gate, so request errors are delivered without healthMonitoring configuration; the gated body is unchanged and the addition is unfenced because Framework has no equivalent call
persisted autogen-key supplier and environment-supplied machineKey values behind NETFRAMEWORK fences (ledger P15)

classic Application_Start failure takes the integrated-mode contract behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: EnsureAppStartCalled latches context.Error into HttpRuntime.InitializationException and rethrows it on every later call, covering requests parked on the app-start lock and requests that reach it past the _appOnStartCalled fast path, and EnsureFirstRequestInit replays the latched exception on later requests, standing in for the FirstRequestInit gate and native-module replay that cover both cases under integrated IIS

the public integrated identity answers as an integrated IIS 10 pool behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences — UsingIntegratedPipeline returns true and IISVersion returns 10.0, the pair reading IV16 measured on the server whose applicationHost.config baseline the port ships — while the internal UseIntegratedPipeline stays false because it selects native notification plumbing; AppVerifier's SyncContextSendOrPostCalledBetweenNotifications assert therefore reads the internal flag, since the NotificationContext it demands is filled only by that plumbing

the integrated-only MapRequestHandler/LogRequest/PostLogRequest event family takes its integrated arm (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): the twelve sync and async accessor gates keep their PlatformNotSupportedException only under NETFRAMEWORK, ApplicationStepManager.BuildSteps adds the three CreateEventExecutionSteps calls with the Log pair inside the early-end jump target, HookupEventHandlersForApplicationAndModules rethrows a refused add_XXX instead of swallowing it off integrated, and HttpContext.RemapHandler asks the step manager (a second range predicate beside IsInBeginRequestStep) and raises Framework's Invoke_before_pipeline_event at or after the map step

the integrated shim batch takes its integrated arm behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: ApplicationStepManager records a notification boundary per CreateEventExecutionSteps call plus the handler-mapping and handler-execution steps and fills a per-step table from it, HttpApplication exposes TryGetCurrentNotification and raises the two pre-send events through RaiseSendResponseEvent, which reports SendResponse and restores HttpContext.Current; HttpContext.CurrentNotification and IsPostNotification read that table and otherwise raise the new Notification_outside_pipeline string added to System.Web.txt; HttpApplication.OnExecuteRequestStep and ThrowIfEventBindingDisallowed drop the UseIntegratedPipeline gate and keep Framework's two init flags; HttpHeaderCollection.Add/Set/Remove gain a request arm whose server-variable mirror reads HttpRequest.ExistingServerVariables rather than the materializing getter, HttpRequest.EnsureHeaders and GetServerVars and HttpServerVarsCollection.Populate stop calling MakeReadOnly, and BuildUrl takes the server name — the host name only, the local port always winning (IV31) — from a Host rewritten through the collection; HttpResponse.AddOnSendingHeaders drops its IIS7WorkerRequest test and WriteHeaders drains the subscription queue before generating headers; and HttpRequest.GetEntireRawContent and HttpBufferlessInputStream.ValidateRequestEntityLength no longer close the connection after an oversize body

the integrated remainder takes its integrated arm behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: ApplicationStepManager.ResumeSteps calls HttpContext.ReportRuntimeErrorIfExists inside the early-end jump when the context carries an error, so the error page and its status are buffered before the Log steps, and HttpRuntime.FinishRequest skips both the app-offline render and the ReportRuntimeError pair when HttpContext.IsRuntimeErrorReported already says so while still running FinalFlushAtTheEndOfRequestProcessing; the four HttpApplication HideRequestResponse gates drop their UseIntegratedPipeline test and InitInternal's classic arm wraps InitModules in the same hiding; HttpServerVarsCollection.Get falls back to HttpRequest.FetchServerVariable for a name the collection does not carry, excluding HTTP_* so a removed header is not resurrected, and FetchServerVariable answers null where there is no worker request; WorkerRequest gains TryGetClientDisconnectedToken and TryAbortConnection beside the WebSocket seam trio, which HttpResponse.ClientDisconnectedToken and HttpRequest.Abort try before their Framework refusal; HttpResponse.SubStatusCode fences out both IIS7WorkerRequest type tests and keeps the _headersWritten refusal; both HttpRequest.InsertEntityBody overloads fence out the refusal and the native call, keeping Framework's argument checks and NeedToInsertEntityBody = false; and HostingEnvironment exposes RaiseStopListening over the existing private OnGlobalStopListening, since the native wait handle SetupStopListeningHandler arms is never signalled off IIS

the integrated fail-fast remainder takes its integrated arm behind !NETFRAMEWORK fences: HostingEnvironment.MaxConcurrentRequestsPerCPU and MaxConcurrentThreadsPerCPU throw unconditionally from both accessors with the new MaxConcurrentPerCPU_not_supported string added to System.Web.txt, which names the property instead of Framework's Requires_Iis_Integrated_Mode message, and the UnsafeIISMethods calls with their S_FALSE/E_INVALIDARG handling stay under NETFRAMEWORK; DefaultAuthenticationModule's Authenticate add accessor throws Framework's own Method_Not_Supported_By_Iis_Integrated_Mode unconditionally while remove stays ungated; and DefaultHttpHandler.BeginProcessRequest throws the same message unconditionally, its port-owned P58 static-content gate having moved to the port-owned StaticFileBridgeHandler subclass that IntegratedHandlers now builds for the native StaticFile handler row
bare `catch {}` reports the discarded exception on the diagnostics choke point (ledger P94)
CLR thread-pool maximum set through ThreadPool.SetMaxThreads instead of the webengine4 export (ledger P95)

StopMonitoringStreamForChanges returns when SupportsChangeNotifications is false (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK): the configuration system stops every stream it marked monitored, marking before it asks the host, so Stop arrives for streams Start never saw

application App_Browsers compiles again: the built-in BrowserCapabilitiesFactory is the pinned base with no ASP.BrowserCapsFactory token-file or GAC probe, and the machine-wide Create/Uninstall throw PlatformNotSupportedException, their service-control, GAC and strong-name code fenced NETFRAMEWORK; top-level browser files sort in DirectoryOrder and custom trees list through BrowserFileListing (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK); parse errors cut the file name at either separator
every hidden check asks HiddenFile, under which a leading dot alone does not hide a name off Windows, direct replacement
ResolveAssembly looks up the simple name of ResolveEventArgs.Name, which .NET gives as a full display name, direct replacement
a null message reads Framework's 'Exception of type ... was thrown.' through a Message override where .NET's ExternalException substitutes its own text (fenced !NETFRAMEWORK)
